predecessors.note: The Mutawakkilite Kingdom of Yemen of Imam Muhammad al-Badr, deposed on 26 September 1962; the same dossier carries the republic as the Yemen Arab Republic.

land.text: the north and east of Yemen, where the royalists made peace with the republic in 1970

successors.note: The page: 'In 1969, sheikhs were brought into the National Assembly'; 'In 1970, Saudi Arabia recognized the Republic' and a ceasefire was effected; the infobox ends the war on 1 December 1970.

correction.text: the border areas held outside the republic in late 1962: Al Jawf and Ma'rib (Harib)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, 1962: late in 1962 the republic was 'in full control of the country, except in some border areas' (a US chargé); royalists held Harib (their commander withdrew to Beihan after the Egyptian takeover in March 1963) and were 'contending to regain some of the positions the Egyptians had taken in the Jawf' in April 1963. The shape (Al Jawf and Ma'rib) is the researcher's reading, with no page giving a boundary.

correction.text: Al Jawf and the Hajjah mountains after the Egyptian takeover of Marib and Harib

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, 1963: Egyptian forces 'occupied Marib' on 25 February and took Harib on 7 March 1963, so the royalists keep Al Jawf and the mountains; the page has royalists holding the surrounding mountains of Hajjah (undated). Runs to 1964: the royalists retook Marib only in July 1965 (reviewer me-10-g).

correction.text: the royalist north and east: Al Jawf, Ma'rib and the Hajjah mountains

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, 1965-1970: the royalists 'occupied Marib on July 16' (the page's 1965 narrative), and the page has 'Both armies controlled most of the north and east of Yemen, including the towns of Harib and Marib' (undated, after 1965). Sa'dah is added as 'controlled by the republicans' only at an undated later point, so the shape keeps Sa'dah out. Egypt held 'a triangle linking Hodeida, Taiz, and San'a' by 1967.

region.text: the border areas outside the republic's control in late 1962

ledger.note: 26 September 1962: the royalists take the field against the republic. Imam Muhammad al-Badr, deposed on 26 September 1962 (Mutawakkilite page), survived; radio broadcasts announced his death on 28 September and he went to Saudi Arabia. The royalists were backed by Saudi Arabia, Jordan, Israel and Britain.
1963: Marib and Harib fall to the Egyptians. 'On February 25, the forces occupied Marib, and on March 7 they took Harib'; the royalist commander at Harib withdrew to Beihan.

16 July 1965: the royalists retake Marib. 'On July 16, they occupied Marib' (after moving into Sirwah in early June and Qaflan on 14 June). The sentence has no year; the page's narrative puts it after 'Between December 1964 and February 1965' and the royalist ambush at Wadi Humaidat on 15 April, so 1965 (reviewer me-10-g corrected 1964 to 1965).
November 1967: the royalists surround Sanaa, take its main airport and cut the Hodeida road; the siege was lifted by February 1968.
February 1968: the siege of Sanaa is lifted; 'the republicans had essentially won the war'.

1 December 1970: the royalist war ends. The infobox gives the war as '26 September 1962 - 1 December 1970'; 'In 1970, Saudi Arabia recognized the Republic', a ceasefire was effected, and the Mutawakkilite monarchy was formally abolished on 1 December 1970 (North Yemen page).

wars.name: North Yemen Civil War

zones.text: the north and east of Yemen
the siege of Sanaa, November 1967 to February 1968

wars.outcome: The republicans, helped by Egyptian troops, outlasted the royalists, who were backed by Saudi Arabia and Jordan; the siege of Sanaa was lifted by February 1968 and Saudi Arabia recognized the republic in 1970.
wars.note: The war is the same as in the north-yemen dossier; the royalists' extent is the researcher's reading of 'most of the north and east of Yemen'.

certainty.note: Front lines of a guerrilla war, moving with each offensive; no page opened gives a boundary.

sources.title: North Yemen Civil War

sources.title: Mutawakkilite Kingdom of Yemen
sources.note: Al-Badr deposed 26 September 1962; the monarchy abolished in 1970.

notes: A rebel state Cliopatria lacks, written from pages opened for north-yemen (North Yemen Civil War, Mutawakkilite Kingdom of Yemen); no extra page was opened. The extent is the weakest part: the Civil War page says 'Both armies controlled most of the north and east of Yemen, including the towns of Harib and Marib' (undated, after 1965), that royalists held the mountains round Hajjah, and that Sa'dah was 'controlled by the republicans' (undated), but gives no boundary, so the shapes (Al Jawf, Ma'rib, the Hajjah governorate) are the researcher's reading at confidence 2 or less. No capital or ruler list: the royalist court's seat is not on the page and Imam al-Badr's rule is already in north-yemen's rulers. A gap-filler should open the Imam al-Badr page for the royalist headquarters (Saudi-border mountains) and the 1970 settlement. The counterpart slug is north-yemen throughout; the Mutawakkilite kingdom is the same dossier as the Yemen Arab Republic.
